target_customer: Affluent individual investors and professionals with multiple accounts and equity, paying for AI wealth management
problem: Human advisors charge 1 to 2 percent of assets and robo-advisors offer generic portfolios, so ordinary investors lack coordinated tax, risk and planning strategies.
business_model: AI wealth management through an SEC-registered investment adviser, advertised at 0% advisory fees with optional paid direct indexing
product_category: AI financial advisor, consumer wealth management

founders.name: Daniel Kobran
founders.background_notes: Co-founder of Paperspace, GPU cloud background, early-stage deep tech investor.

investors: Founder of a quantitative hedge fund

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs account aggregation, tax-loss harvesting, portfolio-backed lending logic, regulated custody integration with Apex and a reliable AI reasoning layer for financial decisions.

defensibility.rationale: SEC registered adviser status and custody integrations plus aggregated user data create friction, but rivals can add AI advice and the founders' pitch is available to any wealth app.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large robo-advisors and AI advice startups (such as YC's Astor from S25) were already targeting the wedge. No incumbent action against ATG found.

market_need_then: The company argues advisory fees of 1 to 2 percent and robo products under $100B AUM leave a gap for personalized AI advice. Demand claims rest on company statements.

branding.domain_note: Product site is becomeautonomous.com, not autonomous.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Calm, confident, personal; stresses autonomy so engaging with complexity is a choice.

branding.brand_signature: Superintelligent financial advisor at 0% advisory fees
branding.community_and_virality: Launch press in January 2026 (Business Insider headline, trade outlets) centred on the founders' prior Paperspace exit and the $15M round.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong founder reputation drives coverage, but the product name is a common word and the service is invitation-only so far.

outcome_analysis: ATG, run by the Paperspace founders, raised a reported $15M pre-seed in January 2026 soon after YC Fall 2025 and runs an invitation-only service through an SEC-registered adviser. It remains early with a small team and no disclosed customers or assets, so its outcome depends on regulatory execution and distribution.
notes: The $15M figure is confirmed by several outlets and a law firm announcement, but the lead investor is not stated and there is no valuation. Preqin lists a separate undisclosed seed from Pioneer Fund in November 2025, unverified and not recorded. Competitors: no source dated near the batch was found, only a 2026 profile listing Wealthfront, Betterment, Vise and Range, so the dated list is empty and those names appear only in takeover_risk_then.
